summary: Enhance your skills in ensuring water access and quality during emergencies. Join our comprehensive training course designed for effective response strategies.
lede: Water access and quality in emergency settings involves planning services that provide adequate, accessible and safe water from source to point of use. For emergency response and water management professionals, the course addresses assessing needs and choosing feasible water sources and treatment options. It also covers field testing, monitoring, managing storage and distribution risks, and using evidence to coordinate decisions and improve services.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals across various sectors involved in emergency response and water management.
audience: Humanitarian program managers and emergency response leads
WASH officers and assistants in field operations
Public health and environmental health practitioners
Government disaster management and county response teams
modules: Emergency Water Reality Check: Why “Access” Is Not Enough
Rapid Needs Assessment and Water Demand Planning
Water Sources in Emergencies: Options, Risks, and Feasibility
Emergency Water Treatment: Choosing What Works Under Pressure
Water Quality Monitoring and Field Testing That Saves Lives
Storage, Distribution, and Safe Water Point Management
Household Water Safety and Behavior in Crisis Conditions
Standards, Accountability, and Quality Assurance Systems
Risk Management: Outbreak Prevention and Contingency Planning
Coordination and Stakeholder Management in Emergency WASH
Inclusion, Protection, and Equity in Water Service Delivery
prerequisites: Participants should have prior experience in emergency response, WASH operations, or related humanitarian work. A basic understanding of water supply and sanitation issues is recommended but not required.
